_comment: Pinned input manifest for the iss-35 brief<->surface cross-check (iss-122). This pins the run's INPUTS, not its findings: two honest runs of the same tier examine the same scope because the doc list, the command and agent rosters, the directions, and the prompt are fixed here rather than chosen per run, but the checkers are LLM agents, so the findings a run returns and their count and classes vary between runs on identical inputs (iss-2608231409595789: three full-tier runs returned 125, 126 and 147). A receipt's failing count is an observation from one run, not a metric to compare across runs. A receipt echoes this file's sha256 as manifestHash; receipt_gate refuses a receipt whose manifestHash does not match this file's actual hash. The detector fills the context's ${commands} and ${agents} from the commands and agents rosters, as it fills ${doc} and ${s.name} for each checker, and starts one checker per briefDocs entry plus one per surfaces entry, a count computed from the two lists and never stored. promptHash is sha256 over context, directionA and directionB joined by blank lines, the templates before any fill, so it changes only when the prompt's wording does. Nothing here that a new surface changes sits on a line every such branch rewrites (iss-2610150526192138): each roster is sorted with one name per line, and briefDocs is ordered by directory and then by file name with its leading chapter number removed, so two branches that each add a surface insert on different lines. TestReleaseGateManifestIsCurrent holds the rosters and the brief-doc list to the tree and to that order, and promptHash to its definition, and TestSurfaceAdditionsMergeCleanly merges two branches that each add a surface. From schemaVersion 2 the release gate holds every finding a receipt records to exactly one disposition, fixed, invalid or deferred, compared byte for byte, and a deferred finding names its own open issue record as "record": "iss-<id>", which no other deferred finding of the release names; a tree whose manifest is schemaVersion 1 keeps the free-text dispositions its receipts were written to. A receipt writer computes the hash at the reviewed commit with `printf 'sha256:'; shasum -a 256 .abcd/development/release-gate/manifest.json | cut -d' ' -f1`; receipt.example.json carries a placeholder in its place, never a literal, because a literal changes with every edit to this file.

tiers.full: both directions over the full brief-doc list; required for a feature (additive) or breaking release
tiers.shallow: Direction B only (surface->brief); sufficient for a patch (fix/internal) release

directions.name: brief->surface
directions.description: per brief doc: verify every surface claim against the shipped binary/tree

directions.name: surface->brief
directions.description: per real surface: find its documented home in the brief

surfaces.name: skills surface
surfaces.probe: list skills/ (abcd ships zero skills; the directory is empty or absent)

prompt.context:
Repo root: the current working directory — use repo-relative paths
throughout, never absolute local paths. Ground truth is the SHIPPED surface,
verified empirically: build the binary (make build produces bin/abcd-<goos>-<arch>)
and run it (`abcd --help` and `abcd <verb> --help`), and list commands/, agents/
and skills/. abcd currently ships ZERO skills — the whole /abcd: surface is
commands under commands/ (${commands})
and agent prompts under agents/ (${agents});
skills/ is empty or absent. The brief chapters that carry surface claims are
pinned in this manifest's briefDocs: .abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/*.md
(the index README included) and the 02-constraints, 05-internals and 06-delivery
chapters that count or enumerate verbs, sub-verbs, agents, hooks and the plugin
tree. That list says where to LOOK, not what may be REPORTED: a surface claim
in any other brief chapter is in scope, and a real surface whose only
documented home lies outside the pinned list is reported with that location.
Report DISCREPANCIES ONLY — where record and reality disagree, or one side is
missing. A brief row explicitly marked staged (its Status column is "staged")
/ probe-only / later-phase is NOT a discrepancy; an unmarked claim about a
surface that does not exist IS. Do not fix anything.
prompt.directionA:
Direction A. Read ${doc} fully. Extract every checkable claim
about the shipped surface (verbs, sub-verbs, flags, skill names, counts,
file layouts, "abcd ships N ..." statements) and verify each against
reality. Return item="${doc}" and the discrepancy list.
prompt.directionB:
Direction B. The real surface "${s.name}" (${s.kind}) exists:
inspect it (${s.probe}). Search the brief's surface chapters for its
documented home (grep .abcd/development/brief/). If no brief row documents
it — or the brief documents it under a wrong name/shape — that is a
discrepancy. Return item="${s.name}" and the discrepancy list (empty if
properly documented).
